I don't have today's price move data for MPC, so I can't tell you whether the stock went up or down or by how much. To explain what drove the move, I'd need to know the direction and magnitude of the price change.

That said, the timing matters here: MPC just reported quarterly earnings and announced a leadership change on the same day (October 29), and those filings likely moved the stock one way or another. The broader refining picture also matters — refineries are running at 94.5 percent capacity, which is healthy, though oil storage is relatively high, which can pressure margins. The gap between US crude (99.64) and world crude (107.03) is wide, which typically benefits US refiners, but analyst caution about Big Oil earnings guidance (noted in the October 29 CNBC piece) suggests the market may be skeptical of forward outlooks in the sector.
